subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should the existing Plugin SDK keyed-store contract gain an explicitly agent-scoped variant, and what runtime-enforced identity and authorization rules must govern access?
rationale: Current main has both durable plugin-global keyed storage and per-agent databases, but repository behavior does not decide whether plugins may access agent-local state, how the active agent is established, or whether a separate cache API should exist.

options.title: Extend the keyed-store seam
options.body: Add an agent-scoped keyed-store factory that derives plugin and agent identity from trusted runtime context while retaining the existing TTL, quota, and storage semantics.

options.title: Keep plugin-global storage only
options.body: Reject a new agent-scoped API and require plugins to use the existing isolated store with documented agent-key namespacing where appropriate.

options.title: Add a separate cache facade
options.body: Introduce `context.cache` as a distinct API with independently specified retention, eviction, authorization, and migration behavior.

recommendation.title: Extend the keyed-store seam
recommendation.body: Add an agent-scoped keyed-store factory that derives plugin and agent identity from trusted runtime context while retaining the existing TTL, quota, and storage semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person most directly to the public Plugin SDK surface where the permanent contract would be exposed.
